pages.title: Quiesce: QuiesceDb, per-rank agents and inode-tree quiescing

features.name: Quiesce sets database (QuiesceDb)
features.description: In-memory database of quiesce sets (set id -> members/roots, state, timeout, expiration, version) owned by one leader MDS per file system; supports include, exclude, reset, release, cancel (by id), cancel-all and query; set ids are user-given or random (one 32-bit mt19937 draw printed with {:x}: up to 8 lowercase hex digits, not zero-padded); sets and excluded members are never garbage collected.
features.notes: Not journaled, not stored in RADOS; lost if all members restart.

features.name: Set and member state machine
features.description: States QUIESCING, QUIESCED, RELEASING (active), RELEASED, EXPIRED, FAILED, CANCELED, TIMEDOUT (terminal). Member QUIESCED only when every member rank reports it; set follows min member state; failure reports propagate; reset resurrects terminal sets.
features.notes: State names are user-visible in fs quiesce output.

features.name: Per-member quiesce timeout and per-set expiration
features.description: timeout: each QUIESCING member must reach QUIESCED within timeout of its inclusion/reset/rollback, else set TIMEDOUT; expiration: max time in QUIESCED/RELEASING measured from reaching QUIESCED, restarted by each successful quiesce-await; defaults 0 (immediate TIMEDOUT/EXPIRED). release does not restart expiration and ignores timeout/expiration arguments.
features.notes: Documented in doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst:1737-1849.

features.name: Await (quiesce-await, release-await, await-for)
features.description: Requests can block until the set is QUIESCED (or RELEASED for release-await); results 0, EPERM, ECANCELED, ETIMEDOUT, EBADF, ENOENT, EINTR (member change), EINPROGRESS (await limit or leadership loss). Successful quiesce-await restarts the expiration timer (watchdog pattern).
features.notes: Awaits on QUIESCED complete before the expiration check of the same pass (barrier with expiration 0).

features.name: Optimistic concurrency with if_version
features.description: if_version must equal the set version or the request fails with ESTALE and is not applied; if_version=0 creates a set only if the id does not exist.
features.notes: Used by CSI-style drivers per doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst:2024-2033.

features.name: Quiesce root sanitization (file:/inode: URIs)
features.description: Roots parsed as URI references, normalized; default scheme file; authority must be fs name (numeric fs id not usable because fs_id is never set, except the literal -1 which equals FS_CLUSTER_ID_NONE); inode: roots must be canonical non-zero u64 but are not actually quiesceable by the MDS agent (become FAILED).
features.notes: Member keys appear as file:/path in output.

features.name: Quiesce DB leader and member selection by monitor
features.description: MDSMonitor writes qdb_cluster_leader (gid of lowest-numbered up:active rank) and qdb_cluster_members (all up:active gids) into each changed MDSMap (encoding ev>=19, JSON qdb_leader/qdb_cluster); every MDS derives membership from it on each map.
features.notes: Stopping ranks are not members.

features.name: Quiesce DB replication protocol
features.description: Leader sends MMDSQuiesceDbListing deltas (sets newer than each peer's acked version) with db_age for clock-free time; agents ack MMDSQuiesceDbAck diff maps; epochs = MDSMap epoch; a leader (new, or existing when a new member joins) bootstraps unknown peers by discovery (listing with set_version 0), adopting a peer DB only if its set_version is higher (then +1), and processes no request or ack until all unknown peers answered; replicas apply only same-epoch listings.
features.notes: MDS<->MDS only; no persistence; resend at most every 1 s and only during leader passes.

features.name: Per-rank QuiesceAgent
features.description: Tracks each root of the local quiesce map, starts one quiesce_path request per root, cancels it on release or root removal, derives actual state (QUIESCING/QUIESCED/RELEASED/EXPIRED/FAILED) and acks diffs to the leader asynchronously; own thread mds-q-agt; TTL is reported but not enforced.
features.notes: Created in MDSRank::active_start.

features.name: Degraded file system handling
features.description: When the MDSMap is degraded the leader injects cancel-all on every map epoch and agents refuse new quiesces with EPERM (member FAILED).

features.name: Tree quiesce (quiesce_path internal request)
features.description: CEPH_MDS_OP_QUIESCE_PATH traverses the root path with DISCOVER|RDLOCK_PATH, spawns quiesce_inode for the root, completes when all in-cache descendants are quiesced, and stays alive holding locks and owning children until killed.
features.notes: Each rank quiesces every root independently in its own cache.

features.name: Per-inode quiesce (quiesce_inode internal request)
features.description: CEPH_MDS_OP_QUIESCE_INODE xlocks quiescelock and rdlocks policylock; on the auth also xlocks filelock and rdlocks auth/link/xattr locks to force cap revocation, then (splitauth) drops them; recurses into in-cache dirfrags with a gather; throttled by a decay counter; fails with EINPROGRESS if another quiesce already holds the inode.
features.notes: Pins every quiesced inode and auth-pins the ones this rank is auth for (replica copies are not auth-pinned) for the quiesce duration.

features.name: quiescelock (CEPH_LOCK_IQUIESCE local lock)
features.description: Per-inode local lock: wrlock implicitly added by acquire_locks for the first cap-related wr/xlock of a request (once per call); xlock held by quiesce_inode; writer-preferring for xlock waiters; release wakes waiters then re-evaluates caps.
features.notes: Ordering: IQUIESCE is CEPH_LOCK_IFIRST. Only skip_quiesce=true callers: quiesce_inode, lock path, Migrator::dispatch_export_dir, MDCache::quarantine_inode, and peer OP_XLOCK/OP_WRLOCK in Server::dispatch_peer_request.

features.name: Drop-all-locks on quiesce wait
features.description: A request that cannot get the quiescelock drops all local and remote locks and auth pins before waiting, so it never holds parent snaplock/policylock while blocked (keeps mksnap possible).
features.notes: Op event 'failed to acquire quiesce lock'.

features.name: Cap masking while quiesced
features.description: While is_quiesced(), issued/allowed/wanted caps are masked to p As Ls Xs Fs Fr Fc Fb; Fx/Fw/Fl/Ax/Lx/Xx are revoked and not reissued; Fb kept to avoid flush storms; async dirop lock-cache caps unavailable because Fx is masked.
features.notes: Writes block in clients waiting for Fw; reads continue.

features.name: Quiesce of inodes that appear later (add_quiesce)
features.description: Any primary inode linked into a dirfrag of a quiesced directory (fetch, replica decode, import, rejoin) gets its own quiesce_inode under the same quiesce_path.

features.name: Fragmentation interplay
features.description: can_fragment refuses quiesced dirs; quiesce aborts in-progress fragmentations that are not all_frozen; fragment_dir aborts itself if it would block on quiescelock; quiesced auth pins block freezing.
features.notes: Aborted split/merge is requeued in the balancer.

features.name: Migration interplay
features.description: export_dir refuses quiesced dirs; quiesce cancels exports up to EXPORT_FREEZING; dispatch_export_dir aborts if it would block on quiescelock; importer NAKs discovery below a quiesced non-auth parent (MDS_TRAVERSE_IMPORT -> EAGAIN).

features.name: ceph.quiesce.block vxattr
features.description: Boolean vxattr stored as inode_t flag F_QUIESCE_BLOCK; quiesce_inode skips such inodes (and their whole subtree) while keeping auth pins; set requires MAY_SET_VXATTR and policylock+snaplock xlock; readable via getvxattr.
features.notes: Clients pass unknown ceph.* xattrs through to the MDS.

features.name: quiesce db admin/tell command
features.description: Command interface to the QuiesceDb with roots, set_id, timeout, expiration, await_for, await, if_version, include/exclude/reset/release/query/cancel, all; json-pretty reply with epoch, leader, set_version, sets; -ENOTTY plus leader gid when not the leader.
features.notes: Runs without mds_lock.

features.name: quiesce path admin command
features.description: Starts quiesce_path on the local rank bypassing the DB; reply with op dump and statistics (inodes, inodes_quiesced, inodes_blocked, inodes_dropped, failed); op persists until op kill.
features.notes: Used by QA.

features.name: lock path admin command
features.description: Test tool that holds arbitrary inode locks (quiesce/snap/policy/file/nest/dft/auth/link/xattr/flock with r/w/x) on a path, optional auth-pin freeze/nonblocking and lifetime.
features.notes: QA only.

features.name: fs quiesce (mgr volumes)
features.description: Maps [group/]subvolume members to subvolume data paths and forwards a quiesce db command to the gid in mdsmap.qdb_leader via libcephfs mds_command2 (one_shot), retrying up to 5 times on ENOTTY using the reply's leader field; output passed through to the user.
features.notes: Options --leader and --with-leader for leader discovery/override.

features.name: Quiesce throttle and heartbeat resets
features.description: quiesce_inode dispatch throttled by DecayCounter (mds_cache_quiesce_decay_rate=1, threshold mds_cache_quiesce_threshold=512K, retry mds_cache_quiesce_sleep=200ms); heartbeat reset every mds_heartbeat_reset_grace=1000 dispatches/kills; mds_cache_quiesce_delay (dev, 0) and mds_cache_quiesce_splitauth (true).

features.name: Quiesce perf counters
features.description: mds_cache.ireq_quiesce_path and mds_cache.ireq_quiesce_inode count finished or killed internal quiesce requests.
features.notes: No gauges for active sets or parked requests.

features.name: MDS compat incompat feature 12 'quiesce subvolumes'
features.description: Part of the default and full MDS compat sets; a daemon must advertise it to be assigned to file systems whose compat includes it.

features.name: Release/cancel via request_kill cascade
features.description: Killing a quiesce_path kills all child quiesce_inode requests recorded in quiesce_ops; each releases quiescelock xlock and policylock rdlock; parked requests are woken before caps are reissued.

features.name: Quarantine reuse of the quiesce walk
features.description: Subvolume quarantine reuses quiesce_path/quiesce_inode with quarantine=true to walk the subtree and revoke caps instead of quiescing.
features.notes: See quarantine page. MDCache::quarantine_inode acquires its cap-related xlocks with skip_quiesce=true, so quarantine mutations are not gated by the quiescelock (a subvolume-root policylock xlock still conflicts with the quiesce policylock rdlock).

features.name: Lock cache invalidation on quiesce
features.description: Taking the quiescelock xlock invalidates lock caches that cached a quiescelock wrlock, revoking async dirop capability from clients.

features.name: Non-active responder callback
features.description: On ranks that are not up:active the agent callback is replaced by a responder that reports QUIESCING roots as FAILED (degraded), QUIESCED (standby-replay) or plain ack; effectively dormant because only up:active ranks are members and the DB is wiped on leaving membership, except for a short window between reset_agent_callback and update_membership in quiesce_cluster_update.

serialization_points.name: Single QuiesceDb leader thread per file system
serialization_points.shared_state: All quiesce sets, version counter, awaits, peer ack table
serialization_points.why_serialized: One authoritative replicated DB with a single version sequence; leader chosen by the monitor
serialization_points.notes: Sets are independent; only the externally addressed single leader (mgr uses mdsmap.qdb_leader) is fixed.

serialization_points.name: Leader bootstrap barrier
serialization_points.why_serialized: A leader (new, or existing when a new member joins) must collect every unknown member's DB before processing requests or acks
serialization_points.notes: No timeout; a silent member blocks the leader until membership changes. leader_upkeep is skipped meanwhile, so set timeouts, expirations and await limits are not evaluated.

serialization_points.name: submit_mutex request/ack/listing queues
serialization_points.why_serialized: Hand-off between messenger/asok/agent threads and the db thread

serialization_points.name: Agent thread processes all roots sequentially
mds_lock for quiesce submit/cancel/send
serialization_points.why_serialized: All cache work and map lookups require mds_lock in C++

serialization_points.name: quiescelock xlock vs implicit wrlocks
serialization_points.shared_state: Admission of mutations needing wr/x locks on cap-related inode locks
serialization_points.why_serialized: Quiesce must stop mutations on the inode and drain in-flight ones
serialization_points.notes: Per-inode granularity is a C++ choice; semantically a subtree-wide write barrier.

serialization_points.name: policylock rdlock held for the quiesce duration
serialization_points.why_serialized: Read F_QUIESCE_BLOCK consistently; holds policy stable during quiesce
serialization_points.notes: Blocks policy vxattr changes cluster-wide (replica rdlocks block auth xlock).

serialization_points.name: Dentry rdlocks along the root path held by quiesce_path
serialization_points.shared_state: Names of path components to the quiesce root
serialization_points.why_serialized: Side effect of path_traverse with MDS_TRAVERSE_RDLOCK_PATH; never dropped
serialization_points.notes: Blocks rename/unlink of path components during quiesce. If a path directory's filelock is cached by a lock cache, the traversal also wrlocks that filelock and (implicitly) its quiescelock for the path lifetime.

serialization_points.name: Client cap revocation wait
serialization_points.shared_state: Client capabilities on each quiesced inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: Clients must stop writing (drop Fw/Fx/Ax/Lx/Xx) before the inode counts as quiesced
serialization_points.notes: Unresponsive clients stall the quiesce until eviction or timeout.

serialization_points.name: Global quiesce dispatch throttle
serialization_points.why_serialized: Limit rate of quiesce_inode dispatch per rank
serialization_points.notes: Shared by all concurrent quiesces on the rank.

serialization_points.name: One internal MDRequest per cached inode
serialization_points.why_serialized: Quiesce state represented as long-lived requests holding locks, all under mds_lock
serialization_points.notes: O(N) requests and held locks; pins cache.

serialization_points.name: Fragment/export vs quiesce mutual exclusion
serialization_points.shared_state: Frozen/freezing dirfrags, auth pins, export state
serialization_points.why_serialized: Avoid deadlock between freezing trees and quiesce_inode ops holding auth pins/locks
serialization_points.notes: Also Migrator.cc:320 quiesce_overdrive_export, Migrator.cc:954 export refusal, MDCache.cc:11893 can_fragment.

serialization_points.name: Cancel-all while degraded
serialization_points.why_serialized: Policy: no consistent quiesce possible while a rank is recovering
serialization_points.notes: Repeated on every map epoch while degraded.

serialization_points.name: Parked requests drop all locks
serialization_points.shared_state: Path locks (snaplock/policylock rdlocks) of waiting requests
serialization_points.why_serialized: Deadlock avoidance with mksnap on the quiesced subvolume
serialization_points.notes: Requests restart lock acquisition from scratch after release.

serialization_points.name: Per-epoch ack round trip
serialization_points.shared_state: Peer ack versions vs membership epoch
serialization_points.why_serialized: Acks only count if tagged with the current MDSMap epoch
serialization_points.notes: Every unrelated MDSMap change delays state progress by an ack round trip.

external_contract.detail: Monitor computes leader = gid of lowest-numbered up:active rank, members = all up:active gids, for every changed MDSMap; encoded at MDSMap extended version ev>=19 and dumped as qdb_leader / qdb_cluster. The MDS must accept these as the quiesce cluster (mgr routes commands to qdb_leader).
Included in MDSMap default/all compat sets; standby daemons are only assigned if their compat is writeable for the fs compat.

MCommand (libcephfs mds_command2, one_shot: the command fails with EPIPE if the MDS connection resets) to mds.<qdb_leader gid> with prefix 'quiesce db', roots (list of subvolume data paths), set_id, timeout, expiration (float s), await_for (float s), await (bool), if_version (int), include/exclude/reset/release/query/cancel/all (bools); extra keys vol_name, members, group_name, leader, with_leader are ignored.

json-pretty object: epoch (int), leader (gid), set_version (int), sets: {set_id: {version, age_ref, state: {name, age}, timeout, expiration, members: {root: {excluded, state: {name, age}}}}}; durations %0.1f seconds; inactive sets omitted unless --all or explicitly requested; returned also on errors; passed verbatim to the CLI user.
Non-leader replies rc -ENOTTY with stdout JSON {epoch, leader}; mgr parses leader and retries up to 5 times.

Negative errno: 0, EINVAL, ENOENT, ESTALE (if_version), EPERM (invalid transition / await in wrong state), EINTR (members changed), ECANCELED, ETIMEDOUT (TIMEDOUT/EXPIRED), EBADF (FAILED), EINPROGRESS (await limit / leadership loss), ENOTTY (not leader), EFAULT (no manager); documented in doc/cephfs/fs-volumes.rst.

Fs/Fr/Fw/Fx/Fl/Ax/Lx/Xx revoked on quiesced inodes (filelock xlock keeps Fc|Fb); only p As Ls Xs Fs Fr Fc Fb reissued while quiesced; client writes block waiting for Fw; Fb revocation is avoided so clients need not write back.
create/mkdir/unlink/rename/setattr/setxattr/O_TRUNC open requests get no reply while the target or parent inode is quiesced; reads, lookups, readdir, flock, cap flushes and capsnap flushes proceed.
Lock caches are invalidated by the quiescelock xlock and Fx is masked on directories, so the client lacks Fx|Fc / Fx|Fr and falls back to synchronous create/unlink.
Set via SETXATTR passthrough of unknown ceph.* names (bool value, MAY_SET_VXATTR), read via GETVXATTR; persisted in inode flags.
Client::_write needs Fw|As and waits in Client::get_caps; ceph-fuse and NFS-Ganesha threads block on writes and on parked metadata requests until release.

external_contract.item: quiesce path / lock path / op kill and op flag points
external_contract.detail: Debug commands used by QA; flag points 'quiesce complete', 'quiesce blocked', 'quiesce complete for non-auth inode', 'quiesce complete for non-auth tree', 'failed to acquire quiesce lock' visible in dump_ops_in_flight.
mds_cache perf counter set; counts finished or killed internal quiesce requests.

rust_implications.implication: Only the edges are contracts: accept the mon-computed qdb_leader/qdb_cluster (or at least make mds.<qdb_leader gid> answer quiesce db and redirect with -ENOTTY + leader), keep the quiesce db argument set, JSON layout, state names, member key format (file:/path), set-id semantics and errno meanings, and advertise compat feature 12. The MMDSQuiesceDb* messages, encodings, epochs and the DB itself are MDS-internal and can be redesigned.

rust_implications.topic: Shard-level write barrier instead of O(N) per-inode requests
rust_implications.implication: With autonomous subvolume shards, a quiesce of a subvolume can be a single shard-level state (an S/X intention lock at the shard root that blocks IX mutation admission) plus a cap-revocation sweep over the shard's cap table, instead of one long-lived MDRequest and lock per cached inode; new inodes loaded during quiesce inherit the barrier from the shard state rather than via add_quiesce.

Mutations blocked by a quiesce must release all locks (especially ancestor snap/policy read locks) before waiting, or snapshot creation on the quiesced subvolume deadlocks; the Rust lock manager should check the quiesce barrier before acquiring any other lock of the operation.

rust_implications.topic: Cover every inode a mutation touches
rust_implications.implication: C++ injects the quiescelock only for the first cap-related lock per acquire_locks call; the Rust design should check the barrier for every shard/inode the transaction plans to modify (cross-shard 2PC participants included).

Reproduce the client-visible cap policy: revoke Fw/Fx/Fl/Ax/Lx/Xx, keep Fc/Fb (avoid forced write-back), keep reads (Fs/Fr) and shared caps, disable async-dirop caps; allow cap flushes, capsnap flushes, flock and mksnap to proceed.

Quiesce sets are independent: process each set (or each shard's membership in a set) on its own executor; avoid a single DB thread and a per-epoch global ack round trip; per-subvolume QoS should not be blocked by quiesce of other subvolumes.

Make quiesce, shard split/merge and shard migration states of the same shard state machine (quiesced shards are not migrated/split, in-flight splits are aborted or completed deterministically) instead of the C++ abort-on-detection heuristics and auth-pin interactions.

C++ cancels all sets while degraded and excludes stopping ranks from membership (gap: subtrees of a stopping rank are not quiesced). A Rust implementation should define quiesce over shard ownership, including shards in migration or held by stopping ranks.

C++ uses leader-relative ages on a wall clock with unsigned durations; Rust can use monotonic clocks per node plus relative ages in replication, keeping the user-visible timeout/expiration/await semantics.

Terminal sets are never collected in C++ and peer messages trust a payload origin field; Rust should bound DB growth (while keeping query --all useful) and authenticate peer identity from the connection.
The DB accepts inode:<ino> roots but the C++ agent cannot quiesce them; a Rust MDS can implement them (shard lookup by ino) without breaking any client.
Quiesce blocks libcephfs threads in get_caps; NFS-Ganesha worker pools stall for the quiesce duration, so expiration defaults and fast release matter for multi-tenant SLAs.

open_questions: Is the once-per-acquire_locks quiescelock injection (need_quiescelock cleared after the first cap-related lock) intentional, and is the possible gap for multi-inode operations crossing a quiesce root acceptable?
Subtrees owned by an up:stopping rank are not covered by any member agent; is this a known limitation?

Release-await success is reported after every agent synchronously killed its quiesce ops (the ack is sent after cancel_request returns), but caps are re-issued and parked requests retried asynchronously; does any consumer expect client I/O to have resumed when release-await returns?

The non-active responder callback (FAILED when degraded, QUIESCED for standby-replay) seems unreachable with the current MDSMonitor membership rule (state == ACTIVE only); is the commented-out broader rule planned?
Should --release apply --timeout/--expiration as the user documentation implies?
Should the DB garbage-collect terminal sets, and is the full-DB replication cost acceptable for long-lived clusters?
Does keeping Fb during quiesce rely on capsnap flushes for snapshot consistency of buffered data (client-side behavior not verified in this page)?
Can a listing rejected by a replica with ESTALE (replica has not yet applied the same MDSMap epoch) delay state progress until the next leader pass, given there is no retransmission timer?
